terminal.absenceSummary: 6 works standing here have no English this project may publish; 2 have only a partly public domain English, not yet taken
absenceReasons: The only English translation is John J. Savage's, in Hexameron, Paradise, and Cain and Abel, Fathers of the Church volume 42 (New York, 1961), reprinted by the Catholic University of America Press in 1977, 1985 and 2010 and still in print. A 1961 United States publication runs 95 years from publication, so it is encumbered until about 2056.
The only English translation of the commentary is C. T. R. Hayward's, Saint Jerome's Hebrew Questions on Genesis, Oxford Early Christian Studies (Clarendon Press, 1995), which is in copyright.

Two English translations exist and both are in copyright: John Hammond Taylor's The Literal Meaning of Genesis, Ancient Christian Writers 41-42 (Newman Press, 1982), and Edmund Hill's On Genesis, The Works of Saint Augustine I/13 (New City Press, 2002). Taylor's runs to 2078 in a life-plus-seventy jurisdiction.
The scholarly translation is Robert C. Hill's, in Commentaries on Genesis 1-3: Severian of Gabala and Bede the Venerable, Ancient Christian Texts (IVP Academic, 2010), which is in copyright.

Calvin B. Kendall's Bede: On Genesis, in the Translated Texts for Historians series (Liverpool University Press, 2008), is the first English translation. Carmen S. Hardin's partial rendering appears in the 2010 Ancient Christian Texts Genesis volume. Both are in copyright.

The only English rendering located is John Litteral's Questions and Answers on Genesis by Augustine, Ambrosiaster, and Alcuin (CreateSpace, 2018), a self-published devotional volume by a living author and firmly in copyright. How much of the Interrogationes it renders could not be established from its catalogue record. No academic translation exists.

No English translation of any date was located. Open Library returns a single record under the name — Silvia Cantelli's Angelomo e la scuola esegetica di Luxeuil (1990), an Italian study — and the Internet Archive returns only sixteenth-century Latin printings of his Enarrationes in libros Regum (1530, 1565) and the Migne volumes. This work appears never to have been put into English.

No English translation of any date was located. The one relevant modern item is Burton Van Name Edwards's The Two Commentaries on Genesis Attributed to Remigius of Auxerre (UMI, 1990), a critical study whose title flags that the Patrologia Latina 131 attribution is itself disputed. Everything else under the name is Latin, French or reference literature.
absencePartials: Partly public domain — Jerome's own PREFACE to the book is public domain: it stands among the Prefaces in the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers second series volume 6 (Fremantle and others, 1893). That is a few paragraphs of introduction and not one of the quaestiones, so it would answer no chapter of Genesis and is recorded rather than landed.

Partly public domain — Roger Pearse published an English of the FIRST homily only at tertullian.org in 2010, dedicated to the public domain in terms that permit free copying. Two things about it decide against landing it without saying so: it is one homily of six, and it is a translation of J. Bareille's 1865 FRENCH rather than of the Greek. A translation of a translation is a third claim again, and this project would have to render it as one — which is possible and has not been done, rather than impossible.
asideNotes: Showing English translation only. This chapter is also held in the author’s own language and Latin translation.
